newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision raises stake in MSG to 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision raises stake in MSG to 50 pct.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp said its wholly-owned Rainbow Programming Holdings Inc subsidiary has paid the remaining balance needed to increase its stake in Madison Square Garden LP to 50 percent from 26.6 percent.
Cablevision said the balance of $168.75 million plus accrued interest was paid to ITT Corp. Cablevision and ITT bought the Madison Square Garden properties in 1995.
Under the agreement between the two companies, Rainbow had until March 17, 1997 to complete its payment of half of the total purchase price.
The MSG properties include the arena complex, the Knicks professional basketball team, the Rangers professional hockey team and the MSG television network.

"Madison Square Garden is New York's premiere sports and entertainment property and a very important strategic asset for Cablevision and Rainbow Programming," said James Dolan, chief executive officer of Cablevision.

The future ownership of the Madison Square Garden properties drew intense speculation last week when ITT, the target of an unwelcome $6.5 billion takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp, said it would consider selling non-core assets to focus on its Sheraton hotel and Caesars casino businesses.

Cablevision, which has right of first refusal to buy ITT's stake in Madison Square Garden, last week declined to comment on whether it would buy the rest. However, sources familiar with the situation said high-level discussions about a sale to Cablevision had taken place although no deal was imminent.
A Cablevision spokesman could not be reached for comment. An ITT spokesman also was not immediately available.
